title: Former Olympic skier Bode Miller’s drug charges dropped by prosecutor’s office
content:
Prosecutors in Idaho have dropped misdemeanor drug charges against former Olympic skier Bode Miller following his arrest early this month.

Lisa A. Blake, the Fremont County prosecuting attorney, said in a statement to The Athletic that while authorities had justification to arrest Miller, her office will not move forward with the case. The prosecutor’s office filed a motion to dismiss on Thursday.

“Although the deputy had sufficient probable cause to arrest Mr. Miller at the beginning of June, we recently received information which resulted in our office determining it is in the interest of justice to dismiss Mr. Miller’s misdemeanor charges,” Blake said via email.

Blake said she will not comment further on the matter “due to it being related to another active case,” but provided no further information.

Miller, 48, was arrested June 6 and charged with possession of a controlled substance and possession of drug paraphernalia. He pleaded not guilty to both charges, according to court records.

Miller’s attorney, Jeromy Stafford, said the skier did not have any drugs on his person when he was arrested. He said Blake’s office decided to dismiss the charges following a conversation between the two sides. Stafford did not disclose what was said in those discussions.

Miller won six medals at five Olympic Games, including gold in the super combined at the 2010 Vancouver Olympics. He also holds the record for most career World Cup wins by an American man, with 33.

Miller retired from the sport in 2017 and was inducted into the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Hall of Fame in 2025.
